text:
maria: Seeing a sudden spike of 502/504s for hosted inference in az3 around 16:09 UTC. Multiple customers reporting timeouts and partial responses. 
jon: Yep, dashboards show latency tail and TCP retransmits on crosslink interface between az3a and az3b. p50 fine, p99 brutal. 
kevin: Any recent deploys? infra-bot did any routing changes? 
infra-bot: deploy-notify: No infra deploys in the last 6 hours to the serving fleet. 
sylvia: I'm seeing provider-level packet reorder and increased SYN retransmit counts on the egress pair. Net graphs: https://dash.redwood/az3/egress/retransmit (short link) 
maria: Customer support ticket #INC-4721 escalating. They included curl repro that stalls at headers. 
support-ops: On the ticket, customer provided tcpdump showing repeated dup ACKs and bursts of out-of-order segments. They said it started after 16:00 local. 
jon: Can someone run a quick traceroute from edge pop to az3 frontend? I want to see AS hops. 
netops: Traceroute from pop-eu-west1 -> az3a: 
```
1  10.1.0.1  1.2 ms
2  203.0.113.45  12.3 ms AS64512
3  198.51.100.22  18.9 ms AS64517
4  198.51.100.73  120.4 ms AS12345 (suspect path)
5  10.2.0.5  121.0 ms
```
netops: Notice the jump at hop 4 with high jitter and AS change. Looks like one provider is shifting traffic through a congested path. 
kevin: Can we fail traffic to the secondary egress pair for az3? What are the failover implications for session affinity? 
sylvia: We can fail to secondary but it will break sticky KV cache for some long-lived sessions; throughput per-instance will drop ~10%. But should reduce retransmits. 
jon: Okay run gradual failover and watch p50/p99. I'll update the canary policy to 50% to start. 
maria: I've told customers we're investigating; they're asking for ETA. 
support-ops: Telling them 30–45m while we validate. 
infra-bot: routing-change: initiating egress shift for az3 to secondary pair (policy: gradual 50% initial). 
netops: Applied route preference change at 16:22 UTC. 
sylvia: Early telemetry: retransmits down 70%, p99 latency improving but still high for some flows. 
kevin: Any signs of BGP AS PATH changes or prepends from provider? 
netops: Provider's looking into a partial backhaul saturation and a BGP path flip. They confirmed a port-level flapping event. 
jon: Mitigation plan: keep secondary active, monitor for 30m, then either fully failover or request provider reroute. Also add short-term TCP keepalive to reduce stalls for affected customers (config push queued). 
maria: Noted — customers updated. One asked about credits/billing for failed requests. 
support-ops: We'll audit failed tokens during window and propose pro-rated credit. Escalating billing-safety to coordinate. 
infra-bot: config-push: TCP keepalive tweak queued to 3s for az3 frontends. Will roll canary 10%. 
kevin: After 20m of stable metrics, we can increase failover to 100% if provider not healed. 
sylvia: Agreed. Also capturing pcap samples and uploading to incident Jira for postmortem. 
netops: Provider reports they've swapped to alternate backhaul at 16:35 UTC; their metrics show queue length dropping. 
john (typo) removed to avoid confusion. 
jon: Metrics now: retransmits ~down to baseline, 502s tail dropping. Keeping monitoring. 
maria: Marking customer ticket as 'investigating' -> 'mitigated' once we confirm 60m stable. 
support-ops: Will follow up with customers and include repro logs and mitigation steps. 
infra-bot: incident-note: mitigation performed (egress failover + TCP tweak). Monitoring window started 16:22 UTC. 
kevin: Postmortem items: look at automatic egress failover thresholds, consider faster failover option for AZ crosslink saturation, and surface provider SLAs for multi-path. 
maria: Thanks all. I'll follow up for postmortem and crediting. :thumbsup:
